p: Thorpe Park is all about the big hitters, and a little strategy can make the difference between a day full of rides and a day full of queuing. Arrive early, decide on your top three must-rides and head straight for them before the crowds build. Many people make a beeline for the newest ride first, so it can pay to go the other way round. Single rider queues, where available, can be a huge time-saver for groups who don't mind being split up for a few minutes.

Look after yourself too. Intense coasters on an empty stomach or straight after a heavy lunch aren't a winning combo, so eat sensibly and drink plenty of water, especially on hot days when the queues can be in full sun. Loose items like phones, sunglasses and hats should be stowed safely before you ride.

Thorpe Park's Fright Nights season around Halloween has become a big draw, with scare mazes and late openings turning the park into something altogether more spooky. If you're a fan of horror, it's a very different way to experience the place, though it's aimed at older teens and adults rather than young children.

Once you've had your fill of thrills, this corner of Surrey has calmer attractions nearby. Runnymede, where the Magna Carta was sealed in 1215, is a short drive away, with riverside meadows and memorials to explore. Windsor, with its famous castle, is close enough for a separate day out, and the Thames path along the river near Chertsey offers a peaceful stroll to bring your heart rate back down.
